lessonTitle: Differences between KOL, rising star, clinical champion and scientific influencer

slides.title: Four Roles, Four Different Engagements
bullets: These four terms are often used interchangeably in mapping work
Each type actually warrants a different kind of engagement
Mixing up the categories wastes time or misses real opportunity

slides.title: The Classic KOL
bullets: Broad, proven influence: publications, guidelines, trial leadership
Wide peer recognition across the therapy area
Engagement centers on mature scientific partnership
Advisory boards and sustained dialogue built over years

slides.title: The Rising Star
bullets: Early or mid-career, trajectory clearly ascending
Publishing increasingly influential work within a sub-specialty
Not yet broadly recognised as an established KOL
Engaging early builds credible relationships before competitors notice

slides.title: The Clinical Champion
bullets: Advocates enthusiastically for a therapy within their own institution
Active in journal clubs, tumor boards, local guideline committees
Narrower geographic scope than a KOL, but high local impact
Credibility comes from being a trusted, present colleague

slides.title: The Scientific Influencer
bullets: Overlaps heavily with the Digital Opinion Leader concept
Influence comes from content, not institutional position or trial leadership
Widely cited papers and framing of how a debate is discussed
Digital content that reaches and engages a wide clinical audience

slides.title: Build a Deliberate, Mixed Portfolio
bullets: Sustained investment in established KOLs
Early relationship-building with credible rising stars
Local engagement with clinical champions to support adoption
Awareness of scientific and digital influencers shaping the conversation

takeaway.title: KOL, rising star, clinical champion and scientific influencer each need a distinct approach
bullets: Confusing the categories leads to misallocated engagement effort
Rising stars and clinical champions matter as much as established KOLs
A deliberate mixed portfolio beats chasing only the most recognisable names
